wind.dial.hint: Drag around the ring, or use − and +. The arrow comes from where the wind blows from. The boat's bow (front) points up.

main.calm: No wind: the mainsail hangs loose, boom {angle}° out
main.furled: Mainsail furled (rolled into the mast): no sail for the wind to push, boom {angle}° out
main.fightingLift: The topping lift holds the boom up, so the main sheet pulls against it (both red). Ease the topping lift, or the main sheet past {pct} %, before the boom can swing out.
jib.calm: No wind: the jib hangs loose, {angle}° out
jib.car: Car on the {side} side of its track
jib.carEnd: Car at the {side} end of its track: easing more lets the top of the jib twist open
jib.furlBlocked: Ease the jib sheet fully (100 %) to furl further (stopped at {pct} % out)
jib.hint: The jib's sheet runs to a car (a slider) on a short track in front of the mast. The car slides to the side away from the wind by itself, so the jib changes sides with no work. Furling rolls the jib around the forestay (the wire to the bow): its back corner moves forward, so the sheet must be eased. At 100 % the sheet is released and the jib can be rolled away completely.
jib.carMiddle: Car in the middle of its track
jib.sheetReleased: Sheet released (100 %): it runs out as the jib rolls up, so the jib flaps
jib.sheetFightsFurl: The jib is rolled up further than this sheet allows: the sheet pulls against the furling line. Ease the sheet to 100 %, or unfurl the jib.
jib.windShadow: With the wind from behind, the mainsail would block the jib's wind and the jib would collapse. The app shows this in a later step.
wheel.turnsClockwise: Wheels turned {turns} turns clockwise: the rudder's back edge goes to starboard, so the boat would turn to starboard (right).
wheel.turnsAnticlockwise: Wheels turned {turns} turns anticlockwise: the rudder's back edge goes to port, so the boat would turn to port (left).
wheel.visualOnly: Only the wheels and the rudder (the blade under the back of the boat) move: the boat itself stays still for now.

clutch.drawingLabel: Clutch banks: tap a clutch to select its rope
clutch.tail.furl: the tail that rolls the mainsail in
clutch.tail.unfurl: the tail that rolls the mainsail out
ropes.strip.label: Selected rope
ropes.strip.empty: Tap a clutch in the drawing, a rope in the 3D view, or a name in the list below to work that rope.
ropes.sharedDetail.ctl_mainsheet: The “Main sheet” clutch (starboard) and the “MAIN SHEET” clutch (port) hold the two ends of the same rope, so it can be worked from either side.
ropes.sharedDetail.ctl_main_furl: The two “Main furling” clutches hold the two tails of one furling line: the left one rolls the mainsail in, the right one rolls it out. “Main outhaul” is hauled together with the “out” tail.
ropes.static.inMastFurling: Not adjusted while sailing: with in-mast furling the main halyard stays hoisted.
ropes.static.notRigged: Not used: no gennaker (a big sail for downwind) is rigged on this boat, so its halyard is parked.

real.stations.label: Where you stand
real.paused: Paused: you can open clutches, wrap turns and switch places. Winching, easing and running ropes wait for Resume, then all happen together.
real.drawing.port: Port station seen from above, forward is up: clutch bank B, the JIB ROLL clutch and the port winch
real.drawing.starboard: Starboard station seen from above, forward is up: clutch bank A and the starboard winch
real.button.label: hold to winch
real.button.aria: Electric winch button: hold it to winch the rope in
real.strip.empty: Tap a clutch (a lock that holds a rope) to work its rope. Drag its lever up to open it, down to close it.
real.strip.elsewhere: This rope's clutch is not here: it is at the {station} station.
real.status.clutchOpen: Clutch open: only what holds the tail stops the rope.
real.status.clutchClosed: Clutch closed: the rope cannot run out (it can still be pulled in).
real.status.offWinch: Not on the winch: nobody holds the tail.
real.status.onWinchJaw: On the winch, {wrap}, tail in the self-tailer (the jaw on top that grips it).
real.status.onWinchHand: On the winch, {wrap}, tail in your hand.
real.status.load: The sail or boom pulls this rope with about {kn} kN.
real.status.loadFighting: This rope pulls against another one (fighting): a very high load.
real.status.noPull: Nothing pulls this rope now (it is slack or the sail is not pulling).
real.status.hold: With the clutch open it is held up to about {kn} kN.
real.motion.running: RUNNING OUT: the pull is more than what holds it.
real.motion.runningPaused: Will run out on Resume: the pull is more than what holds it.
real.note.slipping: Slipping on the drum: not enough turns for this load. Add a turn (about 4 to winch under load).
real.note.wrongWay: Wrapped the wrong way: the drum only turns clockwise, so it just spins with the rope. Take the turns off and wrap clockwise.
real.note.noTurns: No turns on the drum: wrap the rope clockwise first.
real.note.grabby: Easing in jerks: so many turns that your hand cannot feel the rope. Take a turn off to ease smoothly (about 2).
real.note.noLoad: Nothing pulls this rope out: letting go only makes it slack.
real.note.tooHeavy: Too heavy to pull in by hand: put it on the winch.
real.note.cutOutFighting: Winch cut out: too much load. This rope pulls against another one (fighting). Ease the other rope first.
real.note.cutOutEnd: Winch cut out: the rope is fully in and cannot come in further.
real.note.cutOutBlocked: Winch cut out: the sail cannot roll because other ropes are held. Open {clutches} so they can run out.
real.note.cutOutLoad: Winch cut out: too much load. Luff up (turn towards the wind), ease something else, or check for a fighting rope.
real.note.fullyEased: Fully eased: no more rope to let out.
real.notice.clutchClosed: Open the clutch first: a closed clutch never lets a rope out.
real.notice.inSelfTailer: Take the tail out of the self-tailer first, then ease it by hand.
real.notice.winchBusy: One rope per winch: take the other rope off first.
real.notice.winchEmpty: Put a rope on the winch first: drag its tail onto the drum.
real.notice.needTurns: Wrap at least one turn first.
real.notice.staticRope: “{label}” is not worked while sailing: its clutch stays shut.
real.notice.notHere: You are not there: “{label}” is at the {station} station.
real.notice.onWinch: This rope is on the winch: use the winch button.
real.action.easeAria: Ease the rope out by hand (hold to keep easing)
real.helm.hint: The helm: the wheel turns the rudder. Later steps add the engine lever and instruments.
real.how.title: How to work a rope
real.how.1: 1. A clutch (a lock on the rope) holds it when closed. Drag its lever up to open it. A closed clutch still lets the winch pull the rope in.
real.how.2: 2. Drag the rope's tail onto the winch, then circle your finger around the drum clockwise: each circle adds a turn. Anticlockwise takes one off (or wraps it the wrong way). To take the rope off the winch again, circle anticlockwise until it shows 0 turns, then drag the tail back up to its clutch.
real.how.3: 3. Drag the tail into the jaw on top (the self-tailer) so the winch holds it, then hold the winch button to pull the rope in.
real.how.4: 4. To ease (let out): open the clutch, take the tail out of the jaw and drag it away from the winch. About 2 turns ease smoothly; with 4 the rope jerks.
real.how.5: 5. Open a loaded clutch with nothing holding the tail and the rope runs out fast. Take the load on the winch first. You stand at one place at a time: switch with Port, Starboard and Helm.
real.notice.turnsOn: Take the turns off first: circle the drum anticlockwise until it says 0 turns, then drag the rope back to its clutch.
real.drawing.mast: Mast station seen from above, forward is up: the in-mast furling gearbox with its IN/OUT switch and the socket for the winch handle
real.strain.label: load
real.strain.motor: Winch load: about {kn} kN of the {max} kN where it cuts out.
real.strain.handle: The handle needs about {n} N; you can push about {max} N.
real.handle.title: Winch handle
real.handle.hereWinch: The winch handle is in this winch. Circle its grip to crank: clockwise is 1st gear (fast), anticlockwise 2nd gear (slow, about 4 times stronger). Both pull the rope in. To take the handle out, drag its grip onto the handle slot.
real.handle.hereGearbox: The winch handle is in the gearbox. Circle its grip to crank: the main rolls the way the switch says. To take the handle out, drag its grip onto the handle slot.
real.handle.carried: You carry the winch handle. Lay it down (tap the handle slot, or “Leave the handle here”) before you work a rope.
real.handle.awaySocket: The winch handle is in the socket at {station}.
real.handle.cranking: Cranking: {speed} m of rope a second.
real.handleNote.stallGearbox: Too heavy to crank: luff up (turn towards the wind) or ease the main sheet so the sail stops pulling.
real.handleNote.gearboxIn: The main is fully rolled in.
real.handleNote.gearboxOut: The main is fully out. To roll it in, set the switch to IN.
real.handleNote.noRope: No rope on this winch: the handle just turns the empty drum.
real.note.stallFirst: Too heavy for 1st gear: the handle will not turn. Crank anticlockwise instead (2nd gear: slower, about 4 times stronger).
real.note.stallSecond: Too heavy even in 2nd gear: luff up (turn towards the wind), ease something else, or check for a fighting rope.
real.note.stuckFighting: The handle will not turn: this rope pulls against another one (fighting). Ease the other rope first.
real.note.stuckEnd: The handle will not turn: the rope is fully in.
real.note.stuckBlocked: The handle will not turn: the sail cannot roll because other ropes are held. Open {clutches} so they can run out.
real.gearbox.title: In-mast furling gearbox
real.gearbox.caption: Furling gearbox
real.gearbox.switchAria: Gearbox switch, a toggle: IN to the left, OUT to the right. Now {dir}. Tap to flip it.
real.gearbox.mustRunIn: To roll the main in, these must run free (clutch open, not on a winch):
real.gearbox.mustRunOut: To roll the main out, this must run free (clutch open, not on a winch):
real.notice.handleElsewhere: The winch handle is not here: it is at {station}. Go there and take it.
real.notice.handleNotIn: Put the winch handle in the socket first.
real.notice.noSocket: The winch handle fits nowhere here.
real.notice.gearboxNotHere: The gearbox switch is at the {station}.
real.how.6: 6. The winch handle (one on board) is a backup, and every place has a slot where it lies. Tap the slot to take the handle. In a winch it cranks the drum by hand: clockwise is fast but weak, anticlockwise slow but strong. To take it out again, drag its grip onto the slot (the handle only comes out when you let go on the slot). While you carry the handle your hand is full: tap the slot to lay it down before you work a rope. At the Mast it fits the furling gearbox: set the switch to IN, put the handle in and circle its grip to roll the main in, with the “rolls out” line and the outhaul clutches open.
real.practice.title: Practice: the main furling line slips
real.practice.text: Furling the main at 20 kn while the sail still pulls: the “rolls main in” line has only 1 turn on the Starboard winch. Hold the winch button: the line slips. Fix it by hand at the mast: go to Port and take the winch handle, go to Mast, set the switch to IN, put the handle in and circle its grip. The “rolls out” line and the outhaul are already open. (Two turns on the winch, or luffing first, would also work.)
real.status.haulLoad: Pulling it in takes about {kn} kN.
real.gearbox.flipToIn: Flip the switch left to IN (rolls the main in)
real.gearbox.flipToOut: Flip the switch right to OUT (rolls the main out)
real.notice.wrongWayJaw: Wrapped the wrong way, the rope cannot go into the self-tailer. Take the turns off and wrap it clockwise.
real.notice.closedOnRunning: The clutch stopped the running rope. On a real boat, snapping a clutch shut on a loaded rope that is running can strip its cover: take the load on the winch first, then open or close the clutch.
real.notice.handleInHand: You are holding the winch handle: lay it down first (tap the handle slot, or “Leave the handle here”). Remember where you left it.
real.handle.slotAria.rest: Winch handle slot: the handle lies here. Tap to take it.
real.handle.slotAria.carried: Winch handle slot: you carry the handle. Tap to lay it down here.
real.handle.slotAria.socket: Winch handle slot: empty, the handle is in the socket. Drag the handle's grip onto this slot to take it out.
real.handle.slotAria.away: Winch handle slot: empty, the handle is at another place.
real.helm.slot: The helm has a slot for the winch handle too.
